alerts.reason: June revenue grew 3.5% because price/mix added 10.4 percentage points against a 6.9-point volume decline (A, B). I forecast growth above -5% in July–September, then a crossing in October–December as earlier price increases lose their year-over-year effect (D). With the same volume decline, a price/mix contribution of 1.9 points or less would produce the crossing.

Sales fell 3% in the quarter ended July 1. Higher chicken volume helped offset lower volumes in beef, pork and prepared foods (A, B). I expect that support to keep the intervening quarter above -5%, then leveling protein prices and continued volume pressure to widen the year-over-year sales decline to at least 5% in October–December (B, D).

June net sales fell just 0.1% because higher customer prices partly offset lower volume and unfavorable exchange rates. Two plant closures contributed to the volume loss (A, B). I expect pricing to keep July–September above -5%, then provide too little offset to the lost volume to prevent an October–December decline of at least 5%.

June-quarter sales rose 10.5%, but first-half sales fell 0.1%, implying a roughly 19.6% first-quarter decline (A, C). Higher preseason shipments helped drive the June rebound (B). I expect pricing and preseason demand to keep July–September above -5%, with fewer orders left to ship in October–December pushing sales at least 5% below the prior year.

June-quarter sales rose 10%, while order backlog fell 17.7% year over year to $688.8 million (A–C). The remaining backlog was almost twice June-quarter sales. I expect it to sustain shipments above the -5% threshold in July–September, with the smaller order book producing a decline of at least 5% in October–December.

June operating revenue fell 3% even as trucking fuel surcharge revenue fell $41.9 million, helped by strong logistics volume and revenue (A, B, D). I expect logistics volume to keep July–September above -5%, then competitive freight rates and lower surcharges to push the October–December revenue decline to at least 5% (D, E).
